It features a unique blend of set collection and card drafting with the approachable feel of a roll-and-write game. Draft locations from across the continental US as you collect sets of activities and see amazing sights to gain the most points. Boomerang: USA is a stand-alone game in the Boomerang family that plays similarly to the original Boomerang, but has some rules differences and new ways to score, including giving players the opportunity to connect the east and west coasts. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Gameplay 2 Scoring 3 End of the Game 4 Variants Gameplay The game consists of 4 rounds. At the start of each round, deal 7 cards to each player. The others are not used for the round. On your turn, pick a card you want, then pass the rest to the left. All cards drafted are not revealed. After 7 turns, all hands are depleted and drafted cards are scored. Afterwards, shuffle all 28 cards and start a new round. Scoring Throw and Catch: The first card drafted in a round is the throw, and the last card drafted is the catch. If the catch is equal to or higher than the throw, score points equal to the throw. Tourist Sites: Cross out all sights visited each round. At the end of the game, each sight is worth 1 point. If two visited towns have a connecting path, draw it. The first to connect from east coast to west coast scores 7, then 3, then 1. Besides, the first player to visit all towns in a region scores 3 points. Americana: Total all scores on icons. If they are higher than the score last round, score them. Otherwise they are worth 0. Animals: For each pair of animals scores the points marked. Activities: Choose an unscored activity to score the number of icons (0/2/4/7/10/15). End of the Game The game ends after 4 rounds. The player with the highest score wins. If there is a tie, the player with the highest throw and catch wins. Variants Direction Variant: Alternate passing to the left and to the right each round. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] A symbolic 1-rating because of the 'joke' (the creator of the 'joke' and I clearly have a very different sense of humor). For those whom don't know: there is only one 'bigfoot'-symbol of 9 VP. If  you don't know that and you take that card as your first, you'll probably give up a possible throw-catch reward for nothing. I don't find that amusing!

[Rating: 1/10] Light drafting and set collection game akin to Fairy Tale or Sushi Go.   + Card layouts are good, you can easily see icons and letters + Route building in USA > Australia version – Needed fine-tuning on the points, this point salad buffet diffuses focus – Scoring takes more time due to the point salad buffet  – One round too long, 3 is enough for this sort of game – Low interaction never looked at my opponent's tableaus and hate drafting whilst an option isn't really feasible unlike Fairy Tale/Sushi Go

[Rating: 1/10] Terrible drafting game where you can: -get trash hand from which you want 0 or 1 card, -constantly get 0 points from the first "bet" card, and it often doesn't even depend from you, -receive a card which gives 9 VP if you have a pair of such cards, except there is no pair for this card in the whole deck, -play solitaire (not even watching what your opponents do at all) for 2 rounds and become leader after these rounds.

[Rating: 2/10] An absolutely bizarre drafting game, in which it can be revealed in a single round that your drafting decisions were just bad, and can't be recovered because all the cards that you need are gone. Good drafting games are all about pivoting and constant momentum: not getting stuck.

[Rating: 2/10] I remain someone who doesn't really enjoy pick-and-pass card drafting, and whilst this might be an actually-simple implementation of that mechanism unlike often-recommended titles like 7 Wonders, I still didn't find it to be something engaging. (I've also played the Australia and Europe versions and find this much the same; I don't think I prefer one of them in particular.)

[Rating: 4/10] Draft and write, point salad-y thing. I'm already hard pressed to enjoy games in this genre anyway, but the point salad nature of the cards means that there isn't really hate drafting or anything, which just turns it into a pile of pick a thing and whatever. I don't know. It does seem like people like this, and so I guess I just need to assume it isn't for me, and is for someone who wants a more relaxed drafting experience.

[Rating: 5/10] 2021-01-17 - 5 - a simpler, more shallow reedition of a great drafting game. And with misprints affecting the gameplay on top of that. And bigger box, but smaller notebook than the first edition. Missed opportunity.

[Rating: 5/10] The yeti problem clearly makes this an inferior version of the game compared to Australia or Europe.

[Rating: 5/10] Designer: Scott Almes Playing time:  15-30 Min Weight: 1.50 / 5  Publisher: Matagot  [b]COMPLEXITY:[/b] Medium. The rules are simple - is a draft game, much simpler than 7 Wonders, as there is no consideration about demands to take cards. Is more akin to Fairy Tale and Sushi Go, as the only thing that matters is to pick cards to make the most points. Now, about points, the meeting during design of the game surely went this way: Publisher: So, how many things to score do you want? Designer: Yes. There are about 1 million ways to score points in the game. Basically every card you pick will score

[Rating: 5/10] All the different ways of scoring kind of became a mush in my head after a few plays. But I'll say this, the decisions seem to still genuinely matter all the way through a round.  2p is probably more on rails than I realized, with the deck used exactly twice and each player knowing they'll get 4 of the 7 cards from their opening hand. But maybe I like that? i.e. it's more of a "do what you can with what you get" game than a pure drafting game.

[Rating: 5/10] It's fine for a draft and write. Much like the original, nothing makes it stand out overly much for me although you do need to consider what the opponent you are passing your cards to may want (and sometimes draft accordingly...you can't hate draft all the time and expect to win...but if none of the cards do much I'm definitely looking to see what my opponent(s) want and picking accordingly!).
